question: Should Slack intentionally suppress typed preview-owned progress chrome when no reaction can be attached, rather than falling back to a visible progress message?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but the fallback determines whether users receive status information when reaction delivery is unavailable, which is a compatibility and product-policy choice rather than a test-settled detail.

options.title: Approve scoped suppression
options.body: Allow fail-closed behavior only for typed preview-owned progress, preserve configured standalone progress, and require exact-head live proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve visible fallback
options.body: Post the progress message when a reaction cannot be attached, retaining status visibility at the cost of possible channel noise.

options.title: Pause pending policy
options.body: Keep the PR open without landing until Slack progress visibility and reaction-failure behavior have an explicit owner decision.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped suppression
recommendation.body: Allow fail-closed behavior only for typed preview-owned progress, preserve configured standalone progress, and require exact-head live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to recent Slack outbound-delivery review and compatibility decisions.
